ops.name: activity_list
ops.description: Read the interaction log of the whole backlog: every recorded change with its time, source ('ui', 'mcp' or 'cli'), client, operation, entity type and id, the list of touched fields and the changes with their old and new values. An attachment event carries the file name as the value and the attachment id as ref_id. client is the self-declared name/version of the MCP client that made the change, null when the client declared none or the change came from the UI. Supports filters (source, op, entity, from, to) and pagination via limit and offset. Returns: {items, total, ops}, where ops is the list of known operation names.

entity.description: Entity type of the changed object.

project_id.description: Project id: keeps the project's own events, events of its tasks and of its scopes.

from.description: Start of the period as an ISO date-time.

to.description: End of the period as an ISO date-time.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return (default 50, max 200).

offset.description: Number of events to skip, for pagination.

ops.name: attachments_add
ops.description: Attach a file to a task. The file is stored in the media folder of the app, the task keeps only a reference to it. Use it for a raw log, a dump, a config or a dataset that the task needs and that is too big or too volatile for the text. Give either path (a file on the machine where the app runs) or content_base64 (the file content encoded as base64) together with filename. Returns: {item} - the created attachment - {id, task_id, file_name, mime_type, size, created_at, uri, missing, deleted_at}.

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. A bare task number (e.g. '82') is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project, so resolve the project prefix first and pass 'LOG-82'. When nothing matches, the error suggests close ids.

filename.description: The name of the file as it should be shown, with its extension.

path.description: A path to the file on the machine where the app runs. Use it instead of content_base64 when the file is already there.

content_base64.description: The content of the file encoded as base64.

ops.name: attachments_copy
ops.description: Copy an attachment to another task. A new, independent attachment is created from the same bytes: it has its own id and uri, its own row and its own file, so deleting, moving or purging one copy does not touch the other. The copy keeps file_name, mime_type and size of the source and gets the current time as created_at. The source attachment is not changed in any way. Use attachments_move when the file belongs to one task and only its task changes. Fails when the target is the task the attachment is already on, when the target does not exist or is deleted, and when the file is gone from the media folder. Returns: {item} - the created attachment - {id, task_id, file_name, mime_type, size, created_at, uri, missing, deleted_at}.

attachment_id.description: The `id` of an attachment from attachments_list or attachments_deleted_list.

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. A bare task number (e.g. '82') is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project, so resolve the project prefix first and pass 'LOG-82'. When nothing matches, the error suggests close ids.

ops.name: attachments_delete
ops.description: Soft-delete one attachment of a task: the file stays in the media folder and the row keeps its deleted_at, so the attachment can be restored with attachments_restore for 30 days. It disappears from attachments_list and from the task right away. The attachment_id is the `id` field of an item from attachments_list. Returns: the deleted attachment - {id, task_id, file_name, mime_type, size, created_at, uri, missing, deleted_at} with deleted_at set.

attachment_id.description: The `id` of an attachment from attachments_list.

ops.name: attachments_deleted_list
ops.description: List the soft-deleted attachments, newest deletion first. Read-only. Give task_id to list the deleted attachments of one task only, omit it to list every deleted attachment. Soft-deleted files are kept for 30 days, then the file and the row are removed for good. Returns: {items} - every item is {id, task_id, file_name, mime_type, size, created_at, uri, missing, deleted_at} with deleted_at set and task_title - the title of the task the file returns to.

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. A bare task number (e.g. '82') is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project, so resolve the project prefix first and pass 'LOG-82'. When nothing matches, the error suggests close ids.

ops.name: attachments_list
ops.description: List the files attached to one task, without the ones deleted. Read-only. Returns: {items} - every item is {id, task_id, file_name, mime_type, size, created_at, uri, missing, deleted_at}. The uri of an item is an MCP resource holding the bytes of the file: read it with resources/read instead of looking for the file on disk. A file that is gone from the media folder is still listed, with missing set to true.

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. A bare task number (e.g. '82') is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project, so resolve the project prefix first and pass 'LOG-82'. When nothing matches, the error suggests close ids.

ops.name: attachments_move
ops.description: Move an attachment to another task. The attachment keeps its id, its uri and its history, only the task it belongs to changes, so links, ref_id values and resources keep working. A soft-deleted attachment can be moved too, and it lands on the target task restored, with deleted_at cleared: that is the way to bring a deleted file back onto a different task. The file is not copied, the bytes stay where they are, so the move works even when the file is already gone from the media folder. Fails when the target is the task the attachment is already on, when the target does not exist or is deleted, and when the attachment_id is unknown. Use attachments_copy when the file should stay on the source task as well. Returns: {item, previous_task_id, was_deleted} - item is the attachment on its new task, previous_task_id is the task it left, was_deleted tells whether it was soft-deleted before the move.

attachment_id.description: The `id` of an attachment from attachments_list or attachments_deleted_list.

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. A bare task number (e.g. '82') is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project, so resolve the project prefix first and pass 'LOG-82'. When nothing matches, the error suggests close ids.

ops.name: attachments_purge
ops.description: Remove a soft-deleted attachment for good, now instead of waiting for the automatic cleanup: the file in the media folder and the row are gone and cannot be restored. Only works on a soft-deleted attachment. Returns: {id, task_id, file_name, file_removed} - file_removed is false when the file was already gone from the media folder.

attachment_id.description: The `id` of an attachment from attachments_deleted_list.

ops.name: attachments_restore
ops.description: Restore a soft-deleted attachment: it goes back to the task it was attached to, nothing is copied or moved. Find deleted attachments with attachments_deleted_list. Fails when the task is deleted (restore the task first) or when the file is gone from the media folder. Returns: the restored attachment - {id, task_id, file_name, mime_type, size, created_at, uri, missing, deleted_at} with deleted_at set to null.

attachment_id.description: The `id` of an attachment from attachments_deleted_list.

ops.name: attachments_verify
ops.description: Check the files of the attachments: which ones are still in the media folder and which ones are gone. Read-only, soft-deleted attachments are skipped. Returns: {ok, missing} - ok is the list of attachments still in the media folder, missing the ones that are gone. Give task_id to check one task only, omit it to check everything.

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. A bare task number (e.g. '82') is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project, so resolve the project prefix first and pass 'LOG-82'. When nothing matches, the error suggests close ids.

ops.name: backup_create
ops.description: Create a manual backup of the database. Writes a copy into the manual backup folder with a date-time stamp and returns its path. This tool only creates backups; it cannot restore them. Returns: {path} - the path of the written copy.

ops.name: backup_list
ops.description: List the existing database backups: the auto snapshots taken before MCP writes, the daily and weekly copies and the manual ones. Returns: {items} newest first, each item is { kind, name, path, size, mtime }. Restoring is not available here: the user picks the snapshot on the Backups page of the UI, so name the file they should restore.

ops.name: backups_inspect
ops.description: Check a backup before restoring it: the header, the integrity check, the migrations it carries and the number of tasks and projects inside. Not exposed to MCP.

ops.name: backups_restore
ops.description: Replace the whole database with the chosen backup. The current state is copied into the manual folder first and every open tab is reloaded afterwards. Not exposed to MCP.

ops.name: projects_create
ops.description: Create a project. name, project_id and prefix are required. The project_id is a lowercase slug of latin letters, digits and dashes; it is the key of the project in links and in the project_id parameter, and it cannot be changed later. The prefix is 1-6 uppercase letters or digits, it is stored uppercase and starts every task id of the project, and it cannot be changed later either. repo is optional and accepts a git URL; it is stored as host/owner/name. Returns: the created project - {id, name, prefix, repo, created_at, archived_at, task_counts, epic_counts}.

repo.description: Git repository as host/owner/name; a full URL or SSH form is normalized. Optional.

ops.name: projects_get
ops.description: Get a single project by project_id, including task counts by status: task_counts counts non-epic tasks, epic_counts counts epics. scope_counts lists the project's scopes with their task and epic totals. Returns: the project - {id, name, prefix, repo, created_at, archived_at, task_counts, epic_counts} with task_counts, epic_counts and scope_counts.

ops.name: projects_list
ops.description: List projects; set includeArchived to also return archived ones. q filters by a case-insensitive substring of the project name, id, prefix or repo. repo matches the repository exactly after normalization to host/owner/name. Every item carries task_counts and epic_counts: the number of its non-epic tasks and epics per status. Returns: {items} - every item is {id, name, prefix, repo, created_at, archived_at, task_counts, epic_counts} with task_counts and epic_counts.

q.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the project name, id, prefix or repo.

repo.description: Exact repository lookup, canonical host/owner/name. Accepts a git URL and normalizes it.

ops.name: projects_update
ops.description: Rename a project, change its archived flag or set its repository. Pass the fields to change next to project_id (e.g. {project_id: 'spa', name: 'Shop'}); a nested patch object is accepted too. The prefix is immutable — it defines task ids. repo takes host/owner/name or a git URL and null clears it. Returns: the updated project - {id, name, prefix, repo, created_at, archived_at, task_counts, epic_counts}.

repo.description: Git repository as host/owner/name; a full URL or SSH form is normalized. null clears it.
Git repository as host/owner/name; a full URL or SSH form is normalized. null clears it.
Git repository as host/owner/name; a full URL or SSH form is normalized. null clears it.

ops.name: scopes_create
ops.description: Create a scope in a project. A scope groups the tasks of that project; a task points at its scope through scope_id. Returns: the created scope - {id, project_id, name, created_at, task_count, tasks_total, epics_count}.

ops.name: scopes_delete
ops.description: Delete a scope by scope_id; its tasks lose the scope assignment. Pass dry_run: true to preview the deletion - it returns the scope and the ids of the tasks and epics that would lose it, and changes nothing. Returns: {scope, task_ids, epic_ids, dry_run} - the deleted scope and the ids of the tasks and epics that lost it; with dry_run the same report without changing anything.

dry_run.description: Preview the deletion instead of performing it: returns the scope and the ids of the tasks and epics that would lose the scope.

ops.name: scopes_get
ops.description: Get a single scope by scope_id, including its task_count (active non-epic tasks), tasks_total (all non-epic tasks) and epics_count. Returns: the scope - {id, project_id, name, created_at, task_count, tasks_total, epics_count}.

ops.name: scopes_list
ops.description: List scopes, each with task_count (active non-epic tasks assigned, i.e. open/in-progress/blocked), tasks_total (all unfinished and closed non-epic tasks assigned) and epics_count (non-deleted epics assigned). Pass project_id to limit to one project; omit it to list scopes across all projects. Returns: {items} - every item is {id, project_id, name, created_at, task_count, tasks_total, epics_count}.

ops.name: scopes_project_ids
ops.description: List ids of all projects that have at least one scope. Returns: {items} - the list of project ids.

ops.name: scopes_update
ops.description: Rename a scope by scope_id: pass the new name next to scope_id (e.g. {scope_id: 3, name: 'Design'}); a nested patch object {scope_id, patch: {name}} is accepted too. Returns: the updated scope - {id, project_id, name, created_at, task_count, tasks_total, epics_count}.

ops.name: tags_create
ops.description: Add a tag to the dictionary. Tags are a closed list: tasks_create and tasks_update accept only names that are in it. Names are trimmed and lowercased. Calling it on an existing tag changes nothing, and an archived tag is restored. Returns: the tag - {name, archived, created_at}.

ops.name: tags_dictionary
ops.description: List every tag name in the dictionary, including the tags that no task carries yet. Archived tags are excluded: they cannot be assigned. Use tags_list for the counts of the tags in use. Returns: {items} - the tag names, sorted by name.

ops.name: tags_inventory
ops.description: The whole tag dictionary including the archived tags and the tags no task carries, with usage counts. Counts soft-deleted tasks out. Archived tags stay on the tasks that already carry them but cannot be assigned again. `active` counts open, in-progress and blocked tasks, `backlog` counts the backlog ones. Returns: {items, total}, where each item is {name, archived, created_at, count, active, backlog}.

ops.name: tags_list
ops.description: Read the tags in use: every tag with the number of tasks that carry it and the number of open ones. Read-only. Use it before filtering or assigning a tag: the tag list is closed, so tasks_create and tasks_update reject a tag that is not in the dictionary. Archived tags are not listed and cannot be assigned. Accepts the filters project_id and status; soft-deleted tasks are not counted. Returns: {items, total}, where each item is { tag, count, active }, most used first. active counts the tasks that are open, in-progress or blocked: backlog and closed tasks are not counted.

project_id.description: Count only the tags of these projects. Accepts one id or a list of ids.

status.description: Count only the tags of tasks in these statuses. Accepts one status or a list of statuses.

ops.name: tags_rename
ops.description: Rename a tag everywhere: the dictionary entry and every task that carries it. Fails when the new name is already taken. Returns: the tag - {name, archived, created_at}.

ops.name: tags_update
ops.description: Archive or restore a tag by name: pass archived next to name (e.g. {name: 'design', archived: true}); a nested patch object is accepted too. An archived tag keeps the tasks that already carry it, but it disappears from tags_list and cannot be assigned again. Returns: the tag - {name, archived, created_at}.

ops.name: tasks_add_blocker
ops.description: Link two tasks: the task `task_id` becomes blocked by the task `blocked_by` (that is the blocker). Both ids use the full task id form 'PREFIX-NUMBER'. The blocker may live in another project. A task cannot block itself and cycles are rejected. The blocked task keeps its current status: set status 'blocked' with tasks_update yourself. The link is history and stays after the blocker is closed or the task is released, so never remove it for cleanup. Returns: the updated blocked task - {id, project_id, number, title, description, status, priority, is_epic, epic_id, scope_id, source_file, tags, estimate, assignee, due_at, attachments_count, created_at, updated_at, closed_at, closed_reason, blocked_reason, deleted_at, project_name, scope_name, short_description, blocked_by, blocks, relates_to, duplicates, duplicated_by, children_counts} with a changes array describing the link.

task_id.description: Task id of the blocked task in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'). A bare number is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project.

blocked_by.description: Task id of the blocking task in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'). A bare number is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project.

ops.name: tasks_add_link
ops.description: Add a typed link between two tasks. link_type 'relates_to' marks the tasks as related (symmetric: visible from both, one record is stored); 'duplicates' marks `task_id` as a duplicate of `target` (directed). Both ids use the full task id form 'PREFIX-NUMBER'; the target may live in another project. A task cannot relate to or duplicate itself, duplicate cycles are rejected. Returns: the updated source task - {id, project_id, number, title, description, status, priority, is_epic, epic_id, scope_id, source_file, tags, estimate, assignee, due_at, attachments_count, created_at, updated_at, closed_at, closed_reason, blocked_reason, deleted_at, project_name, scope_name, short_description, blocked_by, blocks, relates_to, duplicates, duplicated_by, children_counts} with a changes array describing the link.

task_id.description: Task id of the source task in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'). A bare number is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project.

link_type.description: Link type: 'relates_to' is symmetric (one record, visible from both tasks); 'duplicates' is directed (id duplicates target). Blocking uses tasks_add_blocker instead.

target.description: Task id of the target task in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'). A bare number is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project.

ops.name: tasks_close
ops.description: Close a task by task_id with a reason: 'fixed' → done, 'wontfix' | 'obsolete' | 'duplicate' | 'not-reproduced' → cancelled. 'not-reproduced' marks a report that could not be reproduced. The task_id must use the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'). Closing a task that blocks others releases them from status 'blocked' - every released task returns to the status it had before it was blocked ('open' when that status is unknown), and those tasks are listed in released. The blocking links stay in place as history, so do not remove them afterwards. Returns: the closed task - {id, project_id, number, title, description, status, priority, is_epic, epic_id, scope_id, source_file, tags, estimate, assignee, due_at, attachments_count, created_at, updated_at, closed_at, closed_reason, blocked_reason, deleted_at, project_name, scope_name, short_description, blocked_by, blocks, relates_to, duplicates, duplicated_by, children_counts} with a changes array, a released array and a warnings array, which is not empty when an epic is closed while some of its subtasks are still open. Closing the last open subtask of an epic closes the epic itself with reason 'fixed' and returns it in closed_epic.

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. A bare task number (e.g. '82') is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project, so resolve the project prefix first and pass 'LOG-82'. When nothing matches, the error suggests close ids.

ops.name: tasks_close_many
ops.description: Close several tasks in one call. Each item is applied independently and the response reports ok/error per item; a failing item does not cancel the others. Every task_id must use the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form. Returns: {items, succeeded, failed} - every item is {index, id, ok, task, changes, released, warnings} when it worked and {index, id, ok:false, error:{kind, message}} when it failed, where index is the position in the request list and id is the id of the task.

task_id.description: Full task id, e.g. 'LOG-82'.

ops.name: tasks_comments_add
ops.description: Add a comment to a task. The task id must use the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'). The body is Markdown and formatting is rendered: a short log or config in a fenced block is welcome, source code belongs in the repository. Returns: the created comment - {id, task_id, body, created_at, edited_at, deleted_at}. Editing a comment later keeps its previous text as a revision.

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. A bare task number (e.g. '82') is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project, so resolve the project prefix first and pass 'LOG-82'. When nothing matches, the error suggests close ids.

body.description: Comment text as Markdown for the human reader of the task: what changed and why, in a few sentences. Markdown is rendered, so format it; a short log, config or command output is welcome in a fenced code block when it carries the point. Keep source code in the repository - name the file and describe the algorithm. A raw dump goes to an attachment, and walls of text stay out.

ops.name: tasks_comments_delete
ops.description: Soft-delete a comment by comment_id, the `id` field of an item from tasks_comments_list. The comment disappears from the task, but its id and history stay in the database. Returns: the deleted comment - {id, task_id, body, created_at, edited_at, deleted_at} with deleted_at set.

comment_id.description: The `id` of a comment from tasks_comments_list.

ops.name: tasks_comments_edit
ops.description: Edit the text of a comment by comment_id, the `id` field of an item from tasks_comments_list. The body is Markdown and formatting is rendered, as in tasks_comments_add. The previous text is kept as a revision, so nothing is lost. Returns: the updated comment - {id, task_id, body, created_at, edited_at, deleted_at} with edited_at set.

comment_id.description: The `id` of a comment from tasks_comments_list.

body.description: Comment text as Markdown for the human reader of the task: what changed and why, in a few sentences. Markdown is rendered, so format it; a short log, config or command output is welcome in a fenced code block when it carries the point. Keep source code in the repository - name the file and describe the algorithm. A raw dump goes to an attachment, and walls of text stay out.

ops.name: tasks_comments_list
ops.description: List the comments of a task, oldest first. Deleted comments are hidden. The task id must use the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'). Returns: {items, total} - every item is a comment - {id, task_id, body, created_at, edited_at, deleted_at}.

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. A bare task number (e.g. '82') is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project, so resolve the project prefix first and pass 'LOG-82'. When nothing matches, the error suggests close ids.

ops.name: tasks_create
ops.description: Create a task. Requires project_id and title; description, status, priority, estimate, assignee, due_at, blocked_reason, epic, scope, tags are optional. description is Markdown and formatting is rendered: a short log or config in a fenced block is welcome, source code belongs in the repository. status defaults to 'backlog', where the task waits for a later session, even if the work looks small. Pass 'open' only when you start on it right away, in this same session; 'later' from the user always means backlog. estimate is the size of the task: 'S', 'M' or 'L'. assignee is the person responsible for the task, due_at is its due date (YYYY-MM-DD). blocked_reason is one line of free text explaining a block outside the tracker and is only allowed when status is 'blocked'. epic_id accepts a full epic id (e.g. 'LOG-5') of the same project. scope is optional: pass the scope name (e.g. 'site') or its id as scope_id; a task with neither sits outside the project's scopes, and scopes_create {project_id, name} adds a scope. Tags are optional too, but they come from a closed dictionary: an unknown tag is rejected with the list of existing ones, and tags_create {name} adds a genuinely new tag. source_file names the document or file the task came from; it is provenance only, it is never verified and several tasks may share it. Returns: the created task - {id, project_id, number, title, description, status, priority, is_epic, epic_id, scope_id, source_file, tags, estimate, assignee, due_at, attachments_count, created_at, updated_at, closed_at, closed_reason, blocked_reason, deleted_at, project_name, scope_name, short_description, blocked_by, blocks, relates_to, duplicates, duplicated_by, children_counts} with a warnings array.

description.description: Task description as Markdown: headings, lists, tables, quotes, links and fenced code blocks are rendered in the UI, so use them. A short log, config or command output is welcome in a fenced block when it carries the point; raw dumps go to an attachment instead. Keep source code in the repository - name the file and describe the algorithm. Stay short, no walls of text, and keep the first line a plain sentence: it becomes the one-line preview in lists.

anyOf.description: Epic id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-5'); a bare number such as '5' is unique only inside a project. The epic belongs to the same project as the task. Epics are flat: only a non-epic task carries epic_id, and an epic itself never has one.

scope_id.description: Scope id; it must belong to the same project as the task. Prefer scope (the name) when you know it; scopes_list {project_id} lists the ids.

scope.description: Scope name inside the task's project, e.g. 'ui'. Prefer it over scope_id when you know the name: it is matched case-insensitively, and an unknown name fails with the list of the project's scopes instead of creating one. Passing both scope and scope_id is allowed only when they name the same scope.

source_file.description: File or document the task came from; provenance only, never verified, several tasks may share it.

tags.description: Tags of the task, optional. They are a closed list: see tags_list and create a missing one with tags_create {name}. Names are lowercased.

estimate.description: Size of the task: 'S', 'M' or 'L'. null leaves the task without an estimate.

assignee.description: Person responsible for the task, a free-form name. null leaves the task unassigned.

due_at.description: Due date of the task as YYYY-MM-DD; a full ISO timestamp is accepted and cut to the day. null leaves the task without a due date.

blocked_reason.description: Why the task is blocked, one line of free text. Use it when the blocker is outside the tracker (waiting for a release, an answer, an access). Only allowed on a task with status 'blocked'; null clears it.

ops.name: tasks_create_many
ops.description: Create several tasks in one call. Each item is created independently and the response reports ok/error per item; a failing item does not cancel the others. Items are created in the given order, so task numbers are allocated sequentially. Each item needs its own project_id and title and accepts the same fields as tasks_create, including epic_id as a full epic id of the item's project. Returns: {items, succeeded, failed} - every item is {index, id, ok, task, changes, released, warnings} when it worked and {index, id, ok:false, error:{kind, message}} when it failed, where index is the position in the request list and id is the id of the created task (null for a failed item). changes is empty for a created task, released is empty when nothing was released. Every item carries its own warnings array. Tags are a closed dictionary here as well: an unknown tag fails that item and leaves the others untouched.

description.description: Task description as Markdown: headings, lists, tables, quotes, links and fenced code blocks are rendered in the UI, so use them. A short log, config or command output is welcome in a fenced block when it carries the point; raw dumps go to an attachment instead. Keep source code in the repository - name the file and describe the algorithm. Stay short, no walls of text, and keep the first line a plain sentence: it becomes the one-line preview in lists.

anyOf.description: Epic id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-5'); a bare number such as '5' is unique only inside a project. The epic belongs to the same project as the task. Epics are flat: only a non-epic task carries epic_id, and an epic itself never has one.

anyOf.description: Epic id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-5'); a bare number such as '5' is unique only inside a project. The epic belongs to the same project as the task. Epics are flat: only a non-epic task carries epic_id, and an epic itself never has one.

scope_id.description: Scope id; it must belong to the same project as the task. Prefer scope (the name) when you know it. null clears the scope.

scope.description: Scope name inside the task's project, e.g. 'ui'; matched case-insensitively. null clears the scope. Prefer it over scope_id when you know the name; passing both is allowed only when they name the same scope.

source_file.description: File or document the task came from; provenance only, never verified, several tasks may share it.

tags.description: Tags of the task, optional; an empty array clears them. They are a closed list: see tags_list and create a missing one with tags_create {name}. Names are lowercased.

estimate.description: Size of the task: 'S', 'M' or 'L'. null clears the estimate.

assignee.description: Person responsible for the task, a free-form name. null clears the assignee.

due_at.description: Due date of the task as YYYY-MM-DD; a full ISO timestamp is accepted and cut to the day. null clears the due date.

blocked_reason.description: Why the task is blocked, one line of free text. Use it when the blocker is outside the tracker (waiting for a release, an answer, an access). Only allowed on a task with status 'blocked'; null clears it.

task_id.description: Full task id, e.g. 'LOG-82'.

initialize.instructions: Task backlog server for a single user. Use tasks_*, projects_*, scopes_* and tags_list tools to list, create, update and delete tasks, projects and scopes. tags_list returns the tag dictionary. tasks_revisions_list reads the previous description and comment texts of a task. tasks_deleted_list returns the soft-deleted tasks, the ones that tasks_restore can bring back. attachments_list, attachments_add, attachments_delete and attachments_verify work with the files of a task: they are kept in the media folder, and attachments_verify reports the files that are gone from it. attachments_read returns the file itself, an image as an image block. Every attachment is also a resource: read xboct-log://attachment/{id} with resources/read to get its bytes, take the uri from attachments_list. The resource xboct-log://attachments lists them all. Descriptions and comments are Markdown and formatting is rendered: format them, and put a short log, config or command output in a fenced code block. Keep source code in the repository and describe the algorithm instead, and stay short - no walls of text. A raw log or dump that is really needed belongs in an attachment, not pasted into the text. backup_create makes a manual database backup, backup_list shows the existing snapshots. Restoring a backup is not part of these tools: the user restores a snapshot on the Backups page of the UI, tell them which one. Check isError before reading the payload: a failed call explains the cause in the text, and errors raised by the tool itself also carry structuredContent.error = { kind, message }. Create tasks in batches with tasks_create_many: it answers with one result per item instead of one call per task. All tools accept a single JSON object argument. Task tools address a task by task_id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-42'); attachments address a file by attachment_id, the `id` field of an item from attachments_list.

tools.name: tasks_history
tools.description: Show the change log of one task: when it was changed, from which surface (source: 'ui' or 'mcp'), which MCP client did it (client: the name/version the client declared, null when it declared none) and which fields were touched. Returns: {items, total}, newest first; each item is { ts, source, client, op, fields, changes }. A changed field keeps the old and the new value, a creation lists only the fields set beyond the defaults; an attachment event carries the file name as the value and the attachment id as ref_id. Reads are not logged themselves. The history of a task follows it after a move to another project.

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. A bare task number (e.g. '82') is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project, so resolve the project prefix first and pass 'LOG-82'. When nothing matches, the error suggests close ids.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return (default 50, max 200).

tools.name: activity_list
tools.description: Read the interaction log of the whole backlog: every recorded change with its time, source ('ui', 'mcp' or 'cli'), client, operation, entity type and id, the list of touched fields and the changes with their old and new values. An attachment event carries the file name as the value and the attachment id as ref_id. client is the self-declared name/version of the MCP client that made the change, null when the client declared none or the change came from the UI. Supports filters (source, op, entity, from, to) and pagination via limit and offset. Returns: {items, total, ops}, where ops is the list of known operation names.

entity.description: Entity type of the changed object.

project_id.description: Project id: keeps the project's own events, events of its tasks and of its scopes.

from.description: Start of the period as an ISO date-time.

to.description: End of the period as an ISO date-time.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return (default 50, max 200).

offset.description: Number of events to skip, for pagination.

tools.name: attachments_list
tools.description: List the files attached to one task, without the ones deleted. Read-only. Returns: {items} - every item is {id, task_id, file_name, mime_type, size, created_at, uri, missing, deleted_at}. The uri of an item is an MCP resource holding the bytes of the file: read it with resources/read instead of looking for the file on disk. A file that is gone from the media folder is still listed, with missing set to true.

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. A bare task number (e.g. '82') is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project, so resolve the project prefix first and pass 'LOG-82'. When nothing matches, the error suggests close ids.

tools.name: attachments_deleted_list
tools.description: List the soft-deleted attachments, newest deletion first. Read-only. Give task_id to list the deleted attachments of one task only, omit it to list every deleted attachment. Soft-deleted files are kept for 30 days, then the file and the row are removed for good. Returns: {items} - every item is {id, task_id, file_name, mime_type, size, created_at, uri, missing, deleted_at} with deleted_at set and task_title - the title of the task the file returns to.

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. A bare task number (e.g. '82') is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project, so resolve the project prefix first and pass 'LOG-82'. When nothing matches, the error suggests close ids.

tools.name: attachments_add
tools.description: Attach a file to a task. The file is stored in the media folder of the app, the task keeps only a reference to it. Use it for a raw log, a dump, a config or a dataset that the task needs and that is too big or too volatile for the text. Give either path (a file on the machine where the app runs) or content_base64 (the file content encoded as base64) together with filename. Returns: {item} - the created attachment - {id, task_id, file_name, mime_type, size, created_at, uri, missing, deleted_at}.

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. A bare task number (e.g. '82') is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project, so resolve the project prefix first and pass 'LOG-82'. When nothing matches, the error suggests close ids.

filename.description: The name of the file as it should be shown, with its extension.

path.description: A path to the file on the machine where the app runs. Use it instead of content_base64 when the file is already there.

content_base64.description: The content of the file encoded as base64.

tools.name: attachments_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete one attachment of a task: the file stays in the media folder and the row keeps its deleted_at, so the attachment can be restored with attachments_restore for 30 days. It disappears from attachments_list and from the task right away. The attachment_id is the `id` field of an item from attachments_list. Returns: the deleted attachment - {id, task_id, file_name, mime_type, size, created_at, uri, missing, deleted_at} with deleted_at set.

attachment_id.description: The `id` of an attachment from attachments_list.

tools.name: attachments_restore
tools.description: Restore a soft-deleted attachment: it goes back to the task it was attached to, nothing is copied or moved. Find deleted attachments with attachments_deleted_list. Fails when the task is deleted (restore the task first) or when the file is gone from the media folder. Returns: the restored attachment - {id, task_id, file_name, mime_type, size, created_at, uri, missing, deleted_at} with deleted_at set to null.

attachment_id.description: The `id` of an attachment from attachments_deleted_list.

tools.name: attachments_move
tools.description: Move an attachment to another task. The attachment keeps its id, its uri and its history, only the task it belongs to changes, so links, ref_id values and resources keep working. A soft-deleted attachment can be moved too, and it lands on the target task restored, with deleted_at cleared: that is the way to bring a deleted file back onto a different task. The file is not copied, the bytes stay where they are, so the move works even when the file is already gone from the media folder. Fails when the target is the task the attachment is already on, when the target does not exist or is deleted, and when the attachment_id is unknown. Use attachments_copy when the file should stay on the source task as well. Returns: {item, previous_task_id, was_deleted} - item is the attachment on its new task, previous_task_id is the task it left, was_deleted tells whether it was soft-deleted before the move.

attachment_id.description: The `id` of an attachment from attachments_list or attachments_deleted_list.

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. A bare task number (e.g. '82') is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project, so resolve the project prefix first and pass 'LOG-82'. When nothing matches, the error suggests close ids.

tools.name: attachments_copy
tools.description: Copy an attachment to another task. A new, independent attachment is created from the same bytes: it has its own id and uri, its own row and its own file, so deleting, moving or purging one copy does not touch the other. The copy keeps file_name, mime_type and size of the source and gets the current time as created_at. The source attachment is not changed in any way. Use attachments_move when the file belongs to one task and only its task changes. Fails when the target is the task the attachment is already on, when the target does not exist or is deleted, and when the file is gone from the media folder. Returns: {item} - the created attachment - {id, task_id, file_name, mime_type, size, created_at, uri, missing, deleted_at}.

attachment_id.description: The `id` of an attachment from attachments_list or attachments_deleted_list.

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. A bare task number (e.g. '82') is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project, so resolve the project prefix first and pass 'LOG-82'. When nothing matches, the error suggests close ids.

tools.name: attachments_purge
tools.description: Remove a soft-deleted attachment for good, now instead of waiting for the automatic cleanup: the file in the media folder and the row are gone and cannot be restored. Only works on a soft-deleted attachment. Returns: {id, task_id, file_name, file_removed} - file_removed is false when the file was already gone from the media folder.

attachment_id.description: The `id` of an attachment from attachments_deleted_list.

tools.name: attachments_verify
tools.description: Check the files of the attachments: which ones are still in the media folder and which ones are gone. Read-only, soft-deleted attachments are skipped. Returns: {ok, missing} - ok is the list of attachments still in the media folder, missing the ones that are gone. Give task_id to check one task only, omit it to check everything.

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. A bare task number (e.g. '82') is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project, so resolve the project prefix first and pass 'LOG-82'. When nothing matches, the error suggests close ids.

tools.name: backup_create
tools.description: Create a manual backup of the database. Writes a copy into the manual backup folder with a date-time stamp and returns its path. This tool only creates backups; it cannot restore them. Returns: {path} - the path of the written copy.

tools.name: backup_list
tools.description: List the existing database backups: the auto snapshots taken before MCP writes, the daily and weekly copies and the manual ones. Returns: {items} newest first, each item is { kind, name, path, size, mtime }. Restoring is not available here: the user picks the snapshot on the Backups page of the UI, so name the file they should restore.

tools.name: tasks_add_blocker
tools.description: Link two tasks: the task `task_id` becomes blocked by the task `blocked_by` (that is the blocker). Both ids use the full task id form 'PREFIX-NUMBER'. The blocker may live in another project. A task cannot block itself and cycles are rejected. The blocked task keeps its current status: set status 'blocked' with tasks_update yourself. The link is history and stays after the blocker is closed or the task is released, so never remove it for cleanup. Returns: the updated blocked task - {id, project_id, number, title, description, status, priority, is_epic, epic_id, scope_id, source_file, tags, estimate, assignee, due_at, attachments_count, created_at, updated_at, closed_at, closed_reason, blocked_reason, deleted_at, project_name, scope_name, short_description, blocked_by, blocks, relates_to, duplicates, duplicated_by, children_counts} with a changes array describing the link.

task_id.description: Task id of the blocked task in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'). A bare number is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project.

blocked_by.description: Task id of the blocking task in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'). A bare number is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project.

tools.name: tasks_remove_blocker
tools.description: Remove a blocking link that was recorded by mistake: the task `task_id` is no longer blocked by the task `blocked_by`. Both ids use the full task id form 'PREFIX-NUMBER'. A closed blocker and a task that already left status 'blocked' are not reasons to remove the link: it is the history of the wait and must stay in blocked_by. If no open blocker remains, the blocked task leaves status 'blocked' and returns to the status it had before it was blocked ('open' when that status is unknown). Returns: the updated blocked task - {id, project_id, number, title, description, status, priority, is_epic, epic_id, scope_id, source_file, tags, estimate, assignee, due_at, attachments_count, created_at, updated_at, closed_at, closed_reason, blocked_reason, deleted_at, project_name, scope_name, short_description, blocked_by, blocks, relates_to, duplicates, duplicated_by, children_counts} with a changes array describing the link and the status release.

task_id.description: Task id of the blocked task in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'). A bare number is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project.

blocked_by.description: Task id of the blocking task in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'). A bare number is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project.

tools.name: tasks_add_link
tools.description: Add a typed link between two tasks. link_type 'relates_to' marks the tasks as related (symmetric: visible from both, one record is stored); 'duplicates' marks `task_id` as a duplicate of `target` (directed). Both ids use the full task id form 'PREFIX-NUMBER'; the target may live in another project. A task cannot relate to or duplicate itself, duplicate cycles are rejected. Returns: the updated source task - {id, project_id, number, title, description, status, priority, is_epic, epic_id, scope_id, source_file, tags, estimate, assignee, due_at, attachments_count, created_at, updated_at, closed_at, closed_reason, blocked_reason, deleted_at, project_name, scope_name, short_description, blocked_by, blocks, relates_to, duplicates, duplicated_by, children_counts} with a changes array describing the link.

task_id.description: Task id of the source task in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'). A bare number is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project.

link_type.description: Link type: 'relates_to' is symmetric (one record, visible from both tasks); 'duplicates' is directed (id duplicates target). Blocking uses tasks_add_blocker instead.

target.description: Task id of the target task in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'). A bare number is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project.

tools.name: tasks_remove_link
tools.description: Remove a relates_to or duplicates link between two tasks. Both ids must use the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form. If the link does not exist, returns not_found. Returns: the updated source task - {id, project_id, number, title, description, status, priority, is_epic, epic_id, scope_id, source_file, tags, estimate, assignee, due_at, attachments_count, created_at, updated_at, closed_at, closed_reason, blocked_reason, deleted_at, project_name, scope_name, short_description, blocked_by, blocks, relates_to, duplicates, duplicated_by, children_counts} with a changes array describing the removal.

task_id.description: Task id of the source task in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'). A bare number is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project.

link_type.description: Link type: 'relates_to' is symmetric (one record, visible from both tasks); 'duplicates' is directed (id duplicates target). Blocking uses tasks_add_blocker instead.

target.description: Task id of the target task in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'). A bare number is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project.

tools.name: tasks_comments_list
tools.description: List the comments of a task, oldest first. Deleted comments are hidden. The task id must use the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'). Returns: {items, total} - every item is a comment - {id, task_id, body, created_at, edited_at, deleted_at}.

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. A bare task number (e.g. '82') is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project, so resolve the project prefix first and pass 'LOG-82'. When nothing matches, the error suggests close ids.

tools.name: tasks_comments_add
tools.description: Add a comment to a task. The task id must use the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'). The body is Markdown and formatting is rendered: a short log or config in a fenced block is welcome, source code belongs in the repository. Returns: the created comment - {id, task_id, body, created_at, edited_at, deleted_at}. Editing a comment later keeps its previous text as a revision.

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. A bare task number (e.g. '82') is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project, so resolve the project prefix first and pass 'LOG-82'. When nothing matches, the error suggests close ids.

body.description: Comment text as Markdown for the human reader of the task: what changed and why, in a few sentences. Markdown is rendered, so format it; a short log, config or command output is welcome in a fenced code block when it carries the point. Keep source code in the repository - name the file and describe the algorithm. A raw dump goes to an attachment, and walls of text stay out.

tools.name: tasks_comments_edit
tools.description: Edit the text of a comment by comment_id, the `id` field of an item from tasks_comments_list. The body is Markdown and formatting is rendered, as in tasks_comments_add. The previous text is kept as a revision, so nothing is lost. Returns: the updated comment - {id, task_id, body, created_at, edited_at, deleted_at} with edited_at set.

comment_id.description: The `id` of a comment from tasks_comments_list.

body.description: Comment text as Markdown for the human reader of the task: what changed and why, in a few sentences. Markdown is rendered, so format it; a short log, config or command output is welcome in a fenced code block when it carries the point. Keep source code in the repository - name the file and describe the algorithm. A raw dump goes to an attachment, and walls of text stay out.

tools.name: tasks_comments_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete a comment by comment_id, the `id` field of an item from tasks_comments_list. The comment disappears from the task, but its id and history stay in the database. Returns: the deleted comment - {id, task_id, body, created_at, edited_at, deleted_at} with deleted_at set.

comment_id.description: The `id` of a comment from tasks_comments_list.

tools.name: tasks_options
tools.description: List tasks as a compact picker source: used to fill the epic, blocker and related-task lists of the forms. Without q it returns every task of one project, ordered by number. With q it searches the whole backlog, so a task of another project can be found by its id or title. Returns: {items, total}. The description is left out of the items.

project_id.description: Project id: the tasks of this project only.

q.description: Search over the whole backlog: words are OR-ed, =12 and =LOG-12 match one task exactly.

tools.name: projects_list
tools.description: List projects; set includeArchived to also return archived ones. q filters by a case-insensitive substring of the project name, id, prefix or repo. repo matches the repository exactly after normalization to host/owner/name. Every item carries task_counts and epic_counts: the number of its non-epic tasks and epics per status. Returns: {items} - every item is {id, name, prefix, repo, created_at, archived_at, task_counts, epic_counts} with task_counts and epic_counts.

q.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the project name, id, prefix or repo.

repo.description: Exact repository lookup, canonical host/owner/name. Accepts a git URL and normalizes it.

tools.name: projects_get
tools.description: Get a single project by project_id, including task counts by status: task_counts counts non-epic tasks, epic_counts counts epics. scope_counts lists the project's scopes with their task and epic totals. Returns: the project - {id, name, prefix, repo, created_at, archived_at, task_counts, epic_counts} with task_counts, epic_counts and scope_counts.

tools.name: projects_create
tools.description: Create a project. name, project_id and prefix are required. The project_id is a lowercase slug of latin letters, digits and dashes; it is the key of the project in links and in the project_id parameter, and it cannot be changed later. The prefix is 1-6 uppercase letters or digits, it is stored uppercase and starts every task id of the project, and it cannot be changed later either. repo is optional and accepts a git URL; it is stored as host/owner/name. Returns: the created project - {id, name, prefix, repo, created_at, archived_at, task_counts, epic_counts}.

repo.description: Git repository as host/owner/name; a full URL or SSH form is normalized. Optional.

tools.name: projects_update
tools.description: Rename a project, change its archived flag or set its repository. Pass the fields to change next to project_id (e.g. {project_id: 'spa', name: 'Shop'}); a nested patch object is accepted too. The prefix is immutable — it defines task ids. repo takes host/owner/name or a git URL and null clears it. Returns: the updated project - {id, name, prefix, repo, created_at, archived_at, task_counts, epic_counts}.

repo.description: Git repository as host/owner/name; a full URL or SSH form is normalized. null clears it.
Git repository as host/owner/name; a full URL or SSH form is normalized. null clears it.

tools.name: tasks_revisions_list
tools.description: Read the previous texts of one task: the description and the comment bodies that were replaced by an edit. Read-only. Returns: {items, total}, oldest first; each item is { id, task_id, field, ref_id, body, created_at }, where field is 'description' or 'comment' and ref_id is the id of the edited comment for a comment revision. The current text is not included. Use it to see how a description changed; the activity log only names the touched fields.

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. tags.description: Tags of the task, optional; an empty array clears them. They are a closed list: see tags_list and create a missing one with tags_create {name}. Names are lowercased.

estimate.description: Size of the task: 'S', 'M' or 'L'. null clears the estimate.

assignee.description: Person responsible for the task, a free-form name. null clears the assignee.

due_at.description: Due date of the task as YYYY-MM-DD; a full ISO timestamp is accepted and cut to the day. null clears the due date.

blocked_reason.description: Why the task is blocked, one line of free text. Use it when the blocker is outside the tracker (waiting for a release, an answer, an access). Only allowed on a task with status 'blocked'; null clears it.

tools.name: tasks_close
tools.description: Close a task by task_id with a reason: 'fixed' → done, 'wontfix' | 'obsolete' | 'duplicate' | 'not-reproduced' → cancelled. 'not-reproduced' marks a report that could not be reproduced. The task_id must use the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'). Closing a task that blocks others releases them from status 'blocked' - every released task returns to the status it had before it was blocked ('open' when that status is unknown), and those tasks are listed in released. The blocking links stay in place as history, so do not remove them afterwards. Returns: the closed task - {id, project_id, number, title, description, status, priority, is_epic, epic_id, scope_id, source_file, tags, estimate, assignee, due_at, attachments_count, created_at, updated_at, closed_at, closed_reason, blocked_reason, deleted_at, project_name, scope_name, short_description, blocked_by, blocks, relates_to, duplicates, duplicated_by, children_counts} with a changes array, a released array and a warnings array, which is not empty when an epic is closed while some of its subtasks are still open. Closing the last open subtask of an epic closes the epic itself with reason 'fixed' and returns it in closed_epic.

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. A bare task number (e.g. '82') is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project, so resolve the project prefix first and pass 'LOG-82'. When nothing matches, the error suggests close ids.

tools.name: tasks_close_many
tools.description: Close several tasks in one call. Each item is applied independently and the response reports ok/error per item; a failing item does not cancel the others. Every task_id must use the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form. Returns: {items, succeeded, failed} - every item is {index, id, ok, task, changes, released, warnings} when it worked and {index, id, ok:false, error:{kind, message}} when it failed, where index is the position in the request list and id is the id of the task.

task_id.description: Full task id, e.g. 'LOG-82'.

tools.name: tasks_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete a task by task_id. The task_id must use the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'). Deleting drops the blocker links of the task and detaches it from its epic, so the affected tasks change as well - they are listed in released. Returns: {id, deleted_at, changes, released}.

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. A bare task number (e.g. '82') is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project, so resolve the project prefix first and pass 'LOG-82'. When nothing matches, the error suggests close ids.

tools.name: tasks_restore
tools.description: Restore a soft-deleted task by task_id: clears deleted_at and the task is back on the board. Find deleted tasks with tasks_list(include_deleted: true). The task id must use the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'). Deleting detaches a task from its epic and drops its blocker links — restoring does not bring those back, set them again with tasks_update. Returns: the restored task - {id, project_id, number, title, description, status, priority, is_epic, epic_id, scope_id, source_file, tags, estimate, assignee, due_at, attachments_count, created_at, updated_at, closed_at, closed_reason, blocked_reason, deleted_at, project_name, scope_name, short_description, blocked_by, blocks, relates_to, duplicates, duplicated_by, children_counts}

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. A bare task number (e.g. '82') is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project, so resolve the project prefix first and pass 'LOG-82'. When nothing matches, the error suggests close ids.

tools.name: tasks_move
tools.description: Move a task to another project: project_id is the destination project. The task_id must use the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'). Returns: the moved task - {id, project_id, number, title, description, status, priority, is_epic, epic_id, scope_id, source_file, tags, estimate, assignee, due_at, attachments_count, created_at, updated_at, closed_at, closed_reason, blocked_reason, deleted_at, project_name, scope_name, short_description, blocked_by, blocks, relates_to, duplicates, duplicated_by, children_counts}

task_id.description: Task id in the full 'PREFIX-NUMBER' form (e.g. 'LOG-82'); the prefix is matched case-insensitively, so 'log-82' works too. A bare task number (e.g. '82') is rejected: numbers are unique only inside a project, so resolve the project prefix first and pass 'LOG-82'. When nothing matches, the error suggests close ids.

tools.name: tags_list
tools.description: Read the tags in use: every tag with the number of tasks that carry it and the number of open ones. Read-only. Use it before filtering or assigning a tag: the tag list is closed, so tasks_create and tasks_update reject a tag that is not in the dictionary. Archived tags are not listed and cannot be assigned. Accepts the filters project_id and status; soft-deleted tasks are not counted. Returns: {items, total}, where each item is { tag, count, active }, most used first. active counts the tasks that are open, in-progress or blocked: backlog and closed tasks are not counted.

project_id.description: Count only the tags of these projects. Accepts one id or a list of ids.

status.description: Count only the tags of tasks in these statuses. Accepts one status or a list of statuses.

tools.name: tags_dictionary
tools.description: List every tag name in the dictionary, including the tags that no task carries yet. Archived tags are excluded: they cannot be assigned. Use tags_list for the counts of the tags in use. Returns: {items} - the tag names, sorted by name.

tools.name: tags_create
tools.description: Add a tag to the dictionary. Tags are a closed list: tasks_create and tasks_update accept only names that are in it. Names are trimmed and lowercased. Calling it on an existing tag changes nothing, and an archived tag is restored. Returns: the tag - {name, archived, created_at}.

tools.name: tags_update
tools.description: Archive or restore a tag by name: pass archived next to name (e.g. {name: 'design', archived: true}); a nested patch object is accepted too. An archived tag keeps the tasks that already carry it, but it disappears from tags_list and cannot be assigned again. Returns: the tag - {name, archived, created_at}.

tools.name: tags_rename
tools.description: Rename a tag everywhere: the dictionary entry and every task that carries it. Fails when the new name is already taken. Returns: the tag - {name, archived, created_at}.

tools.name: attachments_read
tools.description: Read the file of one attachment, not only its metadata. An image comes back as an image block, text as text, anything else as base64 in a data URL. Use it to look at a screenshot attached to a task instead of searching the disk for the file. An attachment is at most 20 MB and a big one costs a lot of context, so check size in attachments_list first. A file too big to read can be downloaded from /media/{id} of this server instead.
